exposure: Primary mode of delivery (vacuum extraction, spontaneous vaginal delivery, emergency cesarean section)
outcome: Mode of delivery in second pregnancy (repeat vacuum extraction, emergency cesarean section, spontaneous vaginal delivery)
cohort: 391,160 women in Sweden with two consecutive singleton term live births in cephalic presentation between 1992-2010.
finding: Women with a primary vacuum extraction had an almost five-fold increased risk of repeat vacuum extraction and nearly a three-fold increased risk of emergency cesarean section at second delivery compared to women with a primary spontaneous vaginal delivery.
mod_finding: Nine of ten women who attempted a vaginal birth after a primary vacuum extraction succeeded in having a spontaneous vaginal delivery at second delivery.
